source: Curated from EIA country analysis briefs, operator fact sheets, and public assay data. Figures are nominal.

grades.name: Arab Extra Light
grades.pricingRef: OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index / DME Oman
grades.note: Lightest of the Arab grades, from Berri and Abu Safah fields. Heavily allocated to Asian light-sour configurations.

grades.name: Arab Super Light
grades.pricingRef: OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index / DME Oman
grades.note: Ultra-light condensate stream from the Hawtah Trend. Used to lift heavier blends for direct-distillation yield.

grades.name: Arab Light
grades.pricingRef: OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index / DME Oman
grades.note: Saudi Aramco flagship export grade. Baseline for the Gulf medium-sour complex; largest single crude stream in global trade.

grades.name: Arab Medium
grades.pricingRef: OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index / DME Oman
grades.note: Zuluf and Marjan fields. Higher sulfur than Arab Light, so priced at a discount and targeted at complex cokers.

grades.name: Arab Heavy
grades.pricingRef: OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index / DME Oman
grades.note: Safaniya — the world's largest offshore oil field. The heaviest Arab grade; favored by upgraders with coking capacity.

grades.name: Iranian Light
grades.note: NIOC benchmark export grade. Priced against Dubai; availability sanctioned but widely traded into China and India.

grades.name: Iranian Heavy
grades.note: From Ahvaz, Marun, and Gachsaran. Workhorse of the Iranian export complex; similar cut to Arab Medium.

grades.name: Forozan Blend
grades.note: Offshore Persian Gulf blend (Foroozan, Esfandiar). Medium-sour; exported via Kharg Island.

grades.name: Soroosh
grades.note: Offshore Bahregansar block. Heavy, high-sulfur; requires upgrading yards with deep bottom-of-barrel conversion.

grades.name: Basrah Light
grades.pricingRef: SOMO OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index
grades.note: Southern Iraq, shipped from Basrah Oil Terminal via Hormuz. Historically the marker grade for Iraqi southern exports.

grades.name: Basrah Medium
grades.pricingRef: SOMO OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index
grades.note: Split from the old Basrah stream in 2021 to stabilize the quality bank. Primary Iraqi export grade today.

grades.name: Basrah Heavy
grades.pricingRef: SOMO OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index
grades.note: High-sulfur heavy stream from the south. Priced at a deep discount; targeted at coking refineries in Asia.

grades.name: Kirkuk
grades.note: Northern Iraqi grade evacuated via the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey. Mediterranean-facing, so Brent-priced.

grades.name: Kuwait Export
grades.pricingRef: KPC OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index
grades.note: Blended from Burgan and Raudhatain. KPC's primary long-haul export grade; ships via Mina al-Ahmadi through Hormuz.

grades.name: Murban
grades.note: Onshore ADNOC grade. The only Middle East crude with a fully deliverable futures contract (IFAD). Asian light-sour benchmark.

grades.name: Upper Zakum
grades.note: Offshore giant field co-operated with ExxonMobil, CNPC, and Inpex. Priced against Oman; a close proxy for Arab Light.

grades.name: Das Blend
grades.note: Offshore blend from Umm Shaif and Lower Zakum, staged through Das Island terminal.

grades.name: Umm Lulu
grades.note: Newer offshore ADNOC grade. Similar quality band to Murban; exported separately as ADNOC grade-diversification strategy.

grades.name: Qatar Marine
grades.note: Offshore blend from Al-Shaheen and Maydan Mahzam. Ships via Halul Island through Hormuz.

grades.name: Qatar Land
grades.note: Onshore Dukhan field stream. Lighter and sweeter than Qatar Marine; small but consistently produced.

grades.name: Dukhan / Bahrain
grades.pricingRef: Bapco OSP vs Argus Sour Crude Index
grades.note: Onshore Bahraini crude fed into Bapco's Sitra refinery; a thin export cargo after domestic runs.

grades.name: Oman Export
grades.note: Underlying physical basis of the DME Oman futures contract — the most-looked-at Asian light-medium sour marker.

grades.name: Marib Light
grades.note: Onshore Yemen grade from the Marib-Shabwa basin. Production depressed by civil conflict; cargoes irregular.

grades.name: Masila
grades.note: Hadhramaut governorate. Exports via Ash-Shihr terminal on the Gulf of Aden — outside the Hormuz chokepoint.
